title.narrative: Ma'anshan Cihu River Basin Improvement Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Ma'anshan Cihu River Basin Improvement Project in China is to improve drainage and flood protection capacity in urban areas of Ma'anshan municipality. The project comprises of four components. (1) Cihu River rehabilitation and drainage improvement component will reduce the risk of urban flooding and restore pumping and drainage capacity to discharge the runoff generated by 1 in 10 year storm events through improved storm water collection and discharge facilities along the upper and lower reaches of the Cihu River. (2) Rehabilitation of tributaries and drainage canals component will restore the natural storm drainage function of nearly 27 km of tributaries and canals feeding into the Cihu River by rehabilitating embankments, dredging and removing blockages. It will be designed to ensure that tributaries and canals can handle storm events of 1 in 10 years. (3) Environment management and monitoring component will support the government in developing useful tools for monitoring water quality within the Cihu River watershed and for preventing/mitigating impacts from mine land use that contribute to soil erosion and siltation. (4) Capacity building and project implementation support component will support the overall development of Ma'anshan municipality to coordinate and manage the implementation of the project, including the establishment and operation of a monitoring and evaluation system, safeguards monitoring and the establishment of a project management office.
To improve drainage and flood protection capacity in urban areas of Ma’anshan Municipality

title.narrative: KPI #5 Satisfaction of beneficiaries of improved drainage service and flood protection capacity

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (100% of the target value).</p>

<p>The result included rehabilitation works in upper stream (6.8 km) and downstream (6.2 km) of the Cihu River course plus a section of its branch Lijianwan (1.8 km) downstream. </p>

<p>Information source: PMO/Water resource Bureau. Project progress reports. </p>

<p>Achieved (112% of the target project beneficiaries and 98.2% of the target female beneficiaries)</p>

<p>Direct project beneficiaries were residents, namely the registered and non-registered inhabitants of the Great Cihu River Basin, 49.3% of whom females. The entire population living in the Great Cihu Basin was considered direct beneficiaries given that benefits from flood risk reduction interventions extended beyond the urban areas targeted by the project. </p>

<p>Information source:  Ma'anshan Municipality Yearbook 2020 at http://tjj.mas.gov.cn/tjsj/ndsj/2000569851.html.</p>

<p> </p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: IOI 2-3 Total lengths of Sewers constructed

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (100% +). This indicator was introduced in the September 2017 Restructuring.   </p>

<p>The project funded mainly the works in the trunk network and secondary sewers while the MMG improved also tertiary sewers and household connections. The combined effect resulted in an increased wastewater collection capacity far beyond the initial target value of 4,000 m³/day, which was conservative as it was based on World Bank-financed interventions only (interventions beyond the project could not be guaranteed at the time).</p>

<p>Information source: WWTPs' operation summary.</p>

title.narrative: IOI 2-1 Tributary and drainage canals rehabilitated
IOI 2-1 Tributary and drainage canals rehabilitated

comment.narrative:
<p> Achieved (160% of the original target value and 100% of the revised target value). The target value of this indicatorwas increased in the September 2017 restructuring.</p>

<p>Initially 27 km of tributaries and canals were rehabilitated in Huashan District and High-Tech Zone. After restructuring additional 16.48 km were rehabilitated in Yanghe, Wumushanhe, Heibaitang, Zhenbei  and Hxiaohezha tributaries, and  Zhaoming, Tianranhe South, and Liannong canals.</p>

<p>Source of information: Design information and construction records</p>

title.narrative: IRI 2-1 Tributary and drainage canals rehabilitated
IOI 1-2 Pumping stations upgraded or rehabilitated

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (100% of the target value).</p>

<p>Five pumping stations in the Cihu River lower reach were upgraded by replacingold facilities with new fully equipped modern stations, resulting in an increased capacity of 50 m³/s compared to 34.1 m³/s before the project.</p>

<p>Information source: Design information and construction records. </p>

KPI #5 Satisfaction of beneficiaries of improved drainage service and flood protection capacity
KPI #5 Satisfaction of beneficiaries of improved drainage service and flood protection capacity

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (104% of the target value). This indicator was added during the June 2020 restructuring.</p>

<p>Two rounds of surveys were conducted during November 9 to 12, 2020 with a overall satisfaction rate of 94% among the 402 interviewees (male:234,female:268). The overall satisfaction was estimated as HS+S+0.5MS (counting half of MS in recognition that there were few aspects due to which few interviewees were not 100% satisfied)</p>

<p>Information source: surveys conducted by PMO/PMC/PIUs in August and October of 2020. </p>

title.narrative: KPI #2 Population benefitting from improved drainage
KPI #2 Population benefitting from improved drainage

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (124% of the target value).</p>

<p>The result refers to the population in the sub-catchments along the two sides of Cihu River. People benefited from the improvement and provision of drainage services, especially in the upstream region that used to host mining areas and a residential quarter without connection to the municipal drainage services. In the downstream regions, where an industrial park and an iron steel complex are located, the drainage system was upgraded to a separate system with upscaled sizes. </p>

<p>Information source: Ma'anshan Municipality Yearbook 2020; Water Resource Conservation Bureau. http://tjj.mas.gov.cn/tjsj/ndsj/2000569851.html.</p>

title.narrative: KPI #2 Population benefitting from improved drainage

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved  (100% of the target value).</p>

<p>The area provided with drainage services correspond to the Cihu River's sub-catchment system. Even though the project intervened only in specific locations, the outcome of improved drainage is reflected in the entire sub-catchment system as they are interconnected from the hydraulic standpoint. The project financed drainages activities in Huasan District, Xiushan District, Yushan District, Dangtu County, and Cihu High Tech Zone.</p>

<p>Information source: Ma'anshan Municipal Water Resource Conservation Bureau.</p>

title.narrative: KPI #3 Restoration of storm drainage system for Maanshan

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (over 100%+ of the target value)</p>

<p>Flood protection capacity increased to 1-in-10 -year storm event in tributaries and channels (drainage area) and to 1-in-20-year storm event in the Cihu River. The flood protection improvement resulted from thecombined effect of a higher hydraulic capacity of the Cihu River, upgraded pumping stations, rehabilitated ponds and reduction of benthal sediments in the river.</p>

<p>Information source: Verification Report on Municipal Drainage System Improvement by Shenzhen Water Resources Design Institute. The real case of hydrological data for events of local storms and floods in 2020 summer period.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: KPI #3 Restoration of storm drainage system for Maanshan
KPI #3 Restoration of storm drainage system for Maanshan

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (132% of the target value).</p>

<p>The increment on water detention capacity resulted from the rehabilitation of the main river ( 177,972 m3), two ponds rehabilitation (267,040 m3) and tributaries rehabilitation (437,104 m3). </p>

<p>Information source:  PIUs. and Designing Institute. Verification Report on Municipal Drainage System Improvement by Shenzhen Water Resources Design Institute.</p>

<p>Achieved (100%)</p>

<p>The document 'Environmental Guideline for Mining Region Upstream of Cihu River of Ma'anshanMunicipality' provides  recommendations for the environmental impact assessment from mining activities in the upper reach of the Cihu River and mitigation options. The document was disseminated amongst the regional stakeholders, including the local government agencies, enterprises in the regions, and residents. </p>

<p>Information source: PMO/PIU (Municipal Ecological and Environmental Protection Bureau).</p>

title.narrative: IOI 3-1 Water Quality Monitoring System designed and implemented

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved (100%). </p>

<p>Three automatic water quality monitoring buoy stations were established along Cihu River to monitor water quality parameters. Data are collected in a digital platform from which a Early Warning System (EWS) analyzes changes of water quality and triggers warning signals when threshold values have been passed. EPB staff received training on O&M of the system.</p>
